SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #10
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Change of State? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Change of State.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Change of State.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Change of State.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Invertebrates? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Invertebrates.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Invertebrates.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Invertebrates.

4. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Milk souring

5. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. newton (N)
   C. joule (J)
   D. watt (W)

6. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Only carbon dioxide
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Nitrogen gas only

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Light.

8. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Producers

9. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

10. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Levers as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Levers as simple machines.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Levers as simple machines.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Levers as simple machines.

12. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Composition of Air? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Composition of Air.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Composition of Air.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Composition of Air.

14. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

15. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 100 °C

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Slopes as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Slopes as simple machines.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Slopes as simple machines.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Slopes as simple machines.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Invertebrates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Change of State and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Composition of Air and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

25. In three clear sentences, explain Invertebrates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

26. In three clear sentences, explain Change of State and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
